doctrine: Copywriting is salesmanship in print: every word moves reader toward one action. Core principles: Rule of One (one reader, one idea, one promise, one CTA); match reader's awareness stage (Unaware/Problem/Solution/Product/Most Aware); 531 Method (study 5 high-performing pieces, identify 3 patterns, marry 1 structure); headlines do 80% of work; features tell/benefits sell/transformations close; objections are buying signals; social proof outweighs claims; one CTA per piece; specificity beats vagueness. Awareness Ladder determines headline/lead/proof/CTA strategy per stage. Copy frameworks: PAS (Problem/Agitate/Solve), Rule of One (One Reader/Big Idea/Promise/CTA). Headlines must call out audience, make specific promise, trigger curiosity, state counterintuitive truth, or lead with transformation. Landing pages: above fold (headline/sub-headline/hero image/CTA/social proof); below fold (agitate problem/introduce solution/stack proof/handle objections/restate offer/risk reversal/final CTA). Email structure: subject (2-6 words, curiosity or specificity-driven, lowercase), body (hook/value/CTA, under 100 words cold). Upsell sequence: immediate (deliver + seed), Day 3 (expand result), Day 7 (direct ask). Storytelling structure: struggle/turning point/transformation/reader bridge/offer transition. Operating principle: understand what reader believes, fears, wants; meet them with their own problem language; show the bridge.
gates: Match reader awareness stage before headline
One CTA per piece, no decision paralysis
Use specific numbers over generic claims
workflows: 531 Research Method: find 5 pieces → identify 3 patterns → marry 1 structure
Awareness Ladder positioning: determine stage → match headline/lead → move reader one level
Landing page flow: above fold (hook reader) → below fold (convince) → final CTA
Email upsell sequence: Day 0 (deliver + seed) → Day 3 (expand) → Day 7 (ask)
Story structure: struggle → turning point → transformation → reader bridge → offer
Swipe file building: collect daily → organize by type (headlines/emails/CTAs/proofs) → reference before writing
prompts: What is the reader's current awareness stage?
What is the one big idea this piece centers on?
What does the reader believe about this problem?
What is the single action we want?
What specific transformation will they experience?
What objections will stop them from saying yes?
What does social proof/proof stack exist for this offer?
Does this sentence reinforce the one big idea?
operating_rules: One reader, one big idea, one promise, one CTA
Five times as many people read the headline as the body
Features tell, benefits sell, transformations close
Objections are buying signals, not rejections
Social proof is 10x more persuasive than your claims
Specificity beats vagueness (13.7 lbs in 6 weeks beats 'lose weight fast')
Stories bypass sales resistance; facts tell, stories sell
Copy must meet reader where they are
Short copy outperforms long copy (under 100 words cold, under 200 nurture)
Lowercase email subject lines perform better for cold/personal
Risk reversal (guarantees, trials) removes last barrier
Product sells itself if free asset actually delivers
